Dom John IV ( João ; [ 2 ] [ 3 ] 19 March 1604 – 6 November 1656), also known by the Portuguese as John the Restorer ( João, o Restaurador ), was the King of Portugal from 1640 until his death in 1656. He restored the independence of Portugal from Habsburg Spanish rule [ 1 ] by terminating the 60-year-old Iberian Union in which Portugal and Spain shared the same monarch , and by establishing the House of Braganza on the Portuguese throne.
